clue.text: Theatre worker possibly crediting actors

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the two words could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone in a theatre is perhaps listing the names of the actors in the credits.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the fifteen letters of the two words after the indicator; nicely, this person does choose actors.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional selects performers for roles in a stage or screen production, so is a theatre worker.

clue.text: Breathing space for butterfly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a punctuation mark showing a short pause, as for a breath
second meaning: a common European butterfly with ragged wings and a white mark on the underside

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a rest for a butterfly; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark signals a pause in reading, and the same name belongs to an orange-brown butterfly species.

clue.text: Film Speaker's opening utterance in parliament

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of the word Speaker's

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, whose call is a hoot

explanation.surface: Footage of the Commons Speaker's first words in a parliamentary session.
explanation.walkthrough: Parliament means a group of owls, not Westminster, so the utterance is an owl's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot a scene is to film it with a camera, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Positively well when restricted by trendy diets occasionally

indicators.note: a thing restricted by others is hemmed in between them

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of diets is taken

parts.note: the odd letters of the word
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: A health claim: you feel truly well on fashionable diets, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in large amounts or to a great degree, so it works as an emphatic 'positively'.

clue.text: A lot of tripe upset Pat

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards
a lot of, not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bilge and tripe both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone called Pat was sickened by a large helping of offal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a name but is the adjective, as in a pat answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat reply is slick and too readily given, the same sense as a superficially fluent one.

clue.text: Reserve holiday on QE2 or another ship

indicators.note: in a down answer, one part on another sits above it

parts.note: ice means reserve or coolness of manner
a break is a short holiday
Queen Elizabeth II, whose cipher is ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: Book a cruise on the liner QE2 or some other vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: QE2 is both the old Cunard liner and the queen; the queen gives her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a vessel built to cut through frozen seas, so it is a ship other than the liner.

clue.text: Nurse head cut all together at the same time

definitions.text: all together at the same time

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its tail letter

parts.note: block is slang for the head, as in knock someone's block off

explanation.surface: A nurse cuts everyone's hair in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: Block for head is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means as a single unit, everything handled at once.

clue.text: The Sun? Something clairvoyant will read

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the major arcana in a fortune-teller's pack, not the tabloid
second meaning: a card a clairvoyant lays out and interprets

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper as reading matter for a psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here it is a card in the fortune-telling deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is one of the picture cards of the deck that fortune-tellers lay out and interpret.

clue.text: Britt E's ex struts?

parts.note: reads as the actress Britt Ekland's former partner, a rock singer, swaggering; really the singer's first name with a possessive s, which is also the plural of a bar used as a brace

explanation.surface: The ex-partner of actress Britt Ekland swaggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: Britt Ekland, Swedish actress, lived with the singer Rod Stewart in the 1970s; his name plus 's sounds like the plural of a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rods and struts are both rigid bars used to brace or support a structure.

clue.text: Second leg, be brilliant or rubbish

parts.note: a mo is a moment
on is the leg side in cricket
to shine is to excel

explanation.surface: A sporting second leg: play superbly or flop.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means foolish talk or nonsense, as well as illicit liquor.

clue.text: Left cold wine after first couple of bottles

indicators.note: the wine comes after those two letters
only the opening two letters of bottles are kept

parts.note: red is wine

explanation.surface: White wine left to chill after a couple of bottles had been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left cold' looks like an action on wine, but it means unmoved and uninterested.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that leaves you cold fails to interest you, so you are weary and uninterested.

clue.text: When tense, Charles, say, could be wrong

parts.note: as in the sense 'as I left' means when
Ray Charles was the American soul singer, so Ray is an example of a Charles

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a man named Charles might make a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles is the singer's surname, so this is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off course is to go wrong, as when plans or letters go missing.

clue.text: Give up drinking in flat? Impossible!

parts.note: dry humour is flat and deadpan
out means ruled out, not possible

explanation.surface: An exclamation that quitting booze at home is out of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to stop drinking alcohol, usually after a spell of rehab.

clue.text: Chinese food to appear unexpectedly on list

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to spring up is to appear suddenly
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: A takeaway dish turns up without warning on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: This fried pastry roll with vegetable filling is a familiar Chinese dish.

clue.text: Maybe Charlotte tucked into Christmas pudding

indicators.note: the word sits tucked inside the letters of the two words

parts.note: the letters span the end of Christmas and the start of pudding

explanation.surface: A girl called Charlotte digs into Christmas pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte looks like a person but is a variety of salad potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a variety of potato, and the answer is slang for a potato.

clue.text: Long-term strategy of teacher, with student into pot

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

indicators.note: the student's letter is put into the word for pot

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
L is a learner

explanation.surface: A teacher plans for the long haul, with a student being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: A master plan is a comprehensive scheme guiding action over a long period, a synonym for long-range strategy.

clue.text: Perhaps Hoover up last of grime produced

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Hoover Dam is a famous example of a dam

indicators.note: only the end letter of grime is taken

parts.note: the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A vacuum cleaner sucking up the last of the dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover looks like the vacuum cleaner but is the dam on the Colorado River.
explanation.definitionFit: Made and produced are synonyms, both meaning created or manufactured.

clue.text: Delicacy of virtuous person eating minute steak?

indicators.note: one word eating another holds it inside

parts.note: ST is a saint
wee means tiny
steak is an example of meat, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A saintly person tucking into a minute steak as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: A minute steak is a thin, quickly cooked steak, but minute here means tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word is a confection or candied treat, a small delicacy.

clue.text: This insect used to be first to picnic!

parts.note: was is the past tense of be

indicators.note: the first letter of picnic

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An insect that always arrives first at a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped stinging insect is a notorious picnic pest.

clue.text: Unknown bores in bar ordered starters of Indian samosas and rice dishes

indicators.note: a letter that bores into a word is pushed inside it
the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
maths uses y as an unknown quantity

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: At an Indian restaurant bar, boring people order samosas to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiced South Asian dishes are made with rice, meat or vegetables layered together.

clue.text: Eat sparingly, cut out tons

parts.note: an engine that cuts out dies

explanation.surface: Advice to slim: eat little and cut out the tons of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' looks like advice to skip food; it is the engine sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow a restricted food regimen is to eat sparingly.

clue.text: Compatible and kind, emailed about leaving area

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order
the area's letter leaves the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly, agreeable person sent an email about leaving the area.
explanation.definitionFit: People who think alike share opinions and tastes, making them well suited to each other.

clue.text: Nothing left in wrecked ship from Gdynia?

indicators.note: the two letters go in the rearranged ship
a wrecked ship has its letters broken up and rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Nothing salvaged from a ship wrecked off the port of Gdynia.
explanation.walkthrough: Gdynia is a Baltic port in Poland; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything from a city in Poland can be described with the country's adjective.

clue.text: Pressing remote initially ought to change channel

indicators.note: the letter is pressed into the other letters
change means rearrange the letters
the first letter of remote

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pushing a button on the TV remote should switch channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like TV but is a water channel or gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow open container or gutter carrying water is a kind of channel.

clue.text: Ignore fool behind X with power

indicators.note: the fool's word comes after the other two

parts.note: the multiplication sign is read 'by', as in 3 x 4
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Ignore the idiot standing behind the person marked X, who holds power.
explanation.definitionFit: To go around something without engaging with it is to ignore it.

clue.text: Salute at Pearl Harbour?

parts.note: not a military salute but a spoken greeting in Hawaii, where Pearl Harbor is

explanation.surface: A military salute at the naval base of Pearl Harbor.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearl Harbor makes you think of the navy and war; the clue just wants the Hawaiian greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hawaiian word is used as a greeting and a farewell.

clue.text: Kid rocked, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said aloud and sounds like another

parts.note: rocked and swayed both mean moved to and fro

explanation.surface: A child rocked in a cradle.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid looks like a child, but is soft goatskin leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is fine leather from young goats, and this napped leather is often made from it.

clue.text: In Paris, good day for relationship

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A good day in Paris for a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a link or connection between people, so a relationship.

clue.text: Discover flipper and cap for diving

parts.note: a fin is a flipper

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top letter in a down clue

parts.note: the top letter of the word

explanation.surface: Finding a flipper and a swimming cap for a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon or discover it.

clue.text: Mother-to-be likes going around Marks

indicators.note: the outer words go around the answer, which hides within them

parts.note: the letters run across 'to-be likes', skipping the leading t

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman likes walking about, making her mark.
explanation.definitionFit: These are dagger-shaped printing symbols used to mark spurious passages or footnotes.

clue.text: What Russian church might have — two heads

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bulb-shaped cupola on top of an Orthodox church
second meaning: onion and dome are both slang for the head, so the phrase is literally two heads

explanation.surface: A double-headed design atop a Russian church.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are slang for the head; 'use your onion' is old British slang for think.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian Orthodox churches are famous for bulbous rooftop cupolas shaped like a bulb vegetable.

clue.text: Problem for Forest and Chelsea: muddiest pitches

indicators.note: pitches as a verb means throws, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Nottingham Forest and Chelsea football clubs both suffer from waterlogged grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Forest looks like Nottingham Forest football club, but means woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal blight killed most of Britain's elm trees, a disease of woodland.
